The Monthly Bereavement Support Group Meetings - commenced on 15th October at 8pm in the Newman Institute, Ballina and will meet every second Wedne sday of each month from October 2026 to May 2027 in clusive. A Bereavement Course - presented by Monica Morley, Director of the Knock Shrine Family Centre and Broadcaster at Midwest Radio commences on Tuesday 3rd November at 8pm at The Newman Institute, Ballina. The cost of the course is €60 and will run for the 4 Tuesday nights in November. To book a place please phone 096 720 66. M-PACT is a free eight-week family programme which supports all family members affected by parental su bstance misuse and helps to improve relationships, communic ation and recovery for all. If interested, or would like further information, please contact (071) 9150578 / (085) 8 75 9313 or email

Anyone in hospital / a nursing home - who would like a visit, please let Fr. Martin know. Would you like someone to talk to? Senior Line is Ireland's national telephone service for older people and is open every day of the year 10am-10pm, Freephone 1800 80 45 91. Callers may feel isolated, alone, wish to d iscuss a problem in confidence, or for company during their day. Senior Line's older volunteers are trained to listen, to support , to discuss options & to refer caller to other helpf ul services if necessary. So don't be alone. It helps to share a problem. Collooney Church Conservation – Many thanks to all for your very generous response to the monthly collection. Loose Envelopes – are available in Collooney Church for those who wish to support the project and who do not currently use the offertory envelope system. Also available i n Ballinacarrow for anyone who would like to suppor t the project. The weekly bereavement support group – meets at Knock Shrine on Wednesday mornings at 1 1am in the Family Centre. It provides an opportunity for those who have lost a loved one to meet others who are bereaved and to share and talk about their experience of loss as well as find hope and healing again in their lives. No appointm ent is needed. Please Note – if receiving Holy Communion, it must be consumed immediately and must not be brought back to your seat or brought away. Holy Communion is so sacred a nd so precious that it must always be shown total r espect. Family Carers Ireland - Are you caring for a loved one at home with addit ional needs? A spouse, partner, child, close relative or neighbour? Then you are a family carer Become a member of Family Carers Ireland, the cha rity supporting Ireland’s 500,000+ family carers nationwide.
